_read_this: TEMPLATE. Copy it as .annotepage.json and fill it in.
THIS FILE CONTAINS THE PROJECT KEY, that is to say every note there is.
Whoever reads it reads everything. It is not committed, it is not copied
into a ticket, it is not pasted into a conversation. There is no key
rotation: a leaked key forces you to start from a fresh project,
Keys beginning with an underscore are ignored by the tool: they are there
to be read by whoever opens the file.

review._api: The address of the PHP entry point, api.php included. The same one the browser uses.
review._key: The 43 characters shown by the setup screen, in the browser. No spaces, no decorative dashes. The project id is derived from it: do not write it here. The older name "salt" is still read.
review._mode: "encrypted" (default) or "plain". It is the project's mode, decided at setup.
review._author: The name the assistant signs its replies and its fixes with. It appears in the thread, under the reviewers' eyes. Required in order to write anything at all.
review.author: Assistant
review._origin: The origin to announce to the server, when that server is a RELAY: it refuses every write with no Origin header. Copy here one of the origins declared for this project in the server configuration. Not needed when self-hosted.
review._read_only: true cuts every write: no reply, no fix, no reopening. To be chosen when plugging an assistant onto a review you do not know yet.

_plain_mode_example._why: In plain mode the notes are readable as they are and "curl ?action=text" is enough. You can then declare a project WITH NO key, by giving its id: reading works, writing does not — there is nothing to compute a page index with.
